143	**[IV. Current Pay Stub Practices and Deficiencies]{.underline}**
144	
145	This section provides a detailed audit of the Company\'s current pay stub content for each employee category, mapped against the specific data fields that SB 2847 Phase 1 (effective January 1, 2026) will require. As described below, the Company\'s current pay stubs, generated by the Verdant Payroll Systems platform, contain material deficiencies that must be remediated before the Phase 1 effective date. The remediation is dependent upon a system upgrade by Verdant, which introduces a critical-path timeline constraint.
146	
147	**IV.A. Hourly Warehouse/Operations Workers (2,412 Employees) and Non-Exempt Office/Administrative Staff (315 Employees)**
148	
149	The Company\'s 2,727 hourly and non-exempt employees receive bi-weekly pay stubs generated by Verdant Payroll Systems. The current pay stub format for these employees includes the following data fields:
150	
151	> • Employee name
152	>
153	> • Pay period start and end dates
154	>
155	> • Gross pay (total)
156	>
157	> • Federal income tax withholding
158	>
159	> • State income tax withholding (Illinois)
160	>
161	> • FICA withholding (Social Security and Medicare combined)
162	>
163	> • Net pay (take-home amount)
164	>
165	> • Check number or direct deposit reference number
166	
167	While these fields satisfy basic payroll communication standards and are generally consistent with the Company\'s pre-SB 2847 obligations, the current pay stub format is **missing the following fields** that will be required under SB 2847 Phase 1:
168	
169	**1. Hours worked per day.** The current pay stub does not itemize hours worked on a per-day basis. It reflects only the total hours worked during the bi-weekly pay period as a single aggregate figure. SB 2847 Phase 1 requires that pay stubs for non-exempt employees show hours worked for each day within the pay period, enabling employees to verify daily hour totals against their own records. This is a significant programming and data presentation change, as it requires the pay stub to display up to 14 individual daily hour entries per pay period.
170	
171	**2. Overtime hours separately itemized.** The current pay stub includes overtime compensation within the gross pay figure but does not break out overtime hours as a separate line item. Specifically, the stub does not identify the number of overtime hours worked, the overtime rate of pay, or the total overtime compensation earned during the pay period as distinct from straight-time compensation. SB 2847 Phase 1 requires that overtime hours and the applicable overtime rate be displayed as separate, clearly identified line items on the pay stub. This deficiency is particularly significant given that a substantial number of the Company\'s hourly employees regularly work overtime, especially during peak fulfillment periods.
172	
173	**3. Applicable hourly rate(s).** The current pay stub does not print the employee\'s base hourly rate of pay. For employees with a single, uniform pay rate, this is a relatively straightforward addition. However, an estimated 680 of the Company\'s hourly employees work evening or night shifts and receive shift differentials ranging from \$1.50 to \$2.25 per hour above the base rate. Additionally, some employees split time between facilities or perform tasks at different rate classifications within a single pay period. For these employees, SB 2847 Phase 1 requires that the pay stub separately list each applicable hourly rate and the number of hours worked at each rate. The current system has no capability to display multiple rate breakdowns on a single pay stub.
174	
175	**4. Accrued paid leave balances.** Accrued paid time off (PTO) balances are not currently displayed anywhere on the pay stub. Employees who wish to check their available PTO balance must log into the Cascade HCM Platform separately, navigate to the benefits dashboard, and locate the accrual information there. SB 2847 Phase 1 requires that the employee\'s current accrued paid leave balance --- including any accrued but unused PTO, sick leave, and personal days --- be printed directly on the pay stub as of the end of each pay period. 243	Omnicron engages approximately 740 delivery drivers in Illinois under written Independent Contractor Agreements. 251	**VI.B. Indicators of Control and Direction (Relevant to ABC Test Analysis)**
252	
253	In preparing this audit, I have reviewed the operational realities of the driver engagement model with an eye toward the factors that will be relevant under SB 2847\'s ABC test. The ABC test, as codified in the Act, creates a presumption that a worker is an employee unless the hiring entity can demonstrate that the worker satisfies all three of the following prongs: (A) the worker is free from the control and direction of the hiring entity in the performance of the work; (B) the work is performed outside the usual course of the hiring entity\'s business; and (C) the worker is customarily engaged in an independently established trade, occupation, profession, or business of the same nature as the work performed.
254	
255	I flag the following operational realities that, in my assessment as a human resources professional, present significant concerns under each prong of the new ABC test:
256	
257	**Omnicron-branded vehicles.** Delivery drivers operate vehicles that are leased to them by the Company under a separate Vehicle Lease Agreement. The monthly lease cost is deducted from the driver\'s compensation. These vehicles are painted in the Omnicron Logistics color scheme (dark blue with white accents), bear the Omnicron logo prominently on both sides and the rear, and display the Company\'s customer service telephone number. The vehicles are registered to Omnicron Logistics, Inc. and are insured under the Company\'s commercial fleet policy with Thornhill Risk Advisors. To a customer receiving a delivery, the driver appears in every respect to be an Omnicron employee operating an Omnicron vehicle.
258	
259	**Uniforms.** Drivers are contractually required to wear Omnicron-branded uniforms while performing deliveries. The uniform consists of a dark blue polo shirt with the embroidered Omnicron logo, khaki pants, and an Omnicron-branded jacket for cold weather. The uniforms are purchased by the Company and provided to the drivers at no cost. Drivers are prohibited from wearing clothing bearing the logos of other companies while performing deliveries.
260	
261	**Route assignment.** Delivery routes are generated each day by the Company\'s proprietary routing software (OmniRoute v3.1) and are assigned to specific drivers by the dispatch team at each distribution facility. Drivers do not select their own routes, choose their own delivery stops, or solicit their own customers. The routing software optimizes delivery sequences for efficiency, and drivers are expected to follow the assigned route and stop sequence.
262	
263	**Shift windows.** Drivers are required to be available during scheduled shift windows, which are assigned by the Company\'s dispatch coordinators. The standard shift window is 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM (a twelve-hour window), although actual driving time varies. Drivers must confirm their availability for the following day\'s shift by 4:00 PM the day prior. A driver who declines a shift or fails to confirm availability three or more times within a calendar month may be subject to termination of the Independent Contractor Agreement.
264	
265	**Exclusivity.** Based on a review of the driver files and informal surveys conducted by the HR department, I estimate that approximately **680 of the 740 drivers (91.9%)** work exclusively for Omnicron and do not perform delivery services for any other company. While the Independent Contractor Agreement does not contain a formal exclusivity clause, the practical reality of the scheduling demands (12-hour shift windows, daily availability requirements) makes it extremely difficult for drivers to maintain concurrent delivery engagements with other companies.
266	
267	**Core business.** Delivery is a core component of Omnicron\'s third-party logistics services offering. The Company markets its last-mile delivery capability as a key differentiator to its retail and e-commerce clients. Delivery services represent approximately 31% of the Company\'s total revenue. The work performed by the drivers is not ancillary or peripheral to the Company\'s business --- it is integral to the Company\'s value proposition and operations.
268	
269	I wish to state clearly that the foregoing facts present, in my professional judgment, **significant concerns** regarding the Company\'s ability to satisfy the ABC test with respect to the delivery driver population. I am not rendering a legal opinion --- that task properly falls to Priya Chakravarti and Nora Ellsworth --- but I believe the operational facts described above strongly suggest that the current independent contractor classification may not be sustainable under the new statute. I recommend that legal counsel perform a formal classification analysis under the new ABC test as a matter of urgency.

301	**VII.A. Current Retention Policy**
302	
303	The Company\'s current policy, as set forth in the Omnicron Records Retention Policy (Document No. HR-2021-004, last revised August 2021), requires that payroll records be retained for a period of **four (4) years** from the date of creation. This retention period was established to exceed the then-current Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act requirement of three (3) years and the federal Fair Labor Standards Act requirement of three (3) years for basic payroll records (and two (2) years for certain supplemental records such as collective bargaining agreements and time clock records).
304	
305	SB 2847, under its Phase 2 provisions effective April 1, 2026, extends the mandatory Illinois retention period for payroll records to **seven (7) years**. The statute defines \"payroll records\" broadly to include pay stubs, wage notices, time and attendance records, records of deductions, records of accrued leave, and any other documentation related to the calculation and payment of wages.
306	
307	The Company\'s current four-year retention policy therefore falls **three years short** of the new statutory requirement. Records that are currently being destroyed after four years (i.e., records from the fifth, sixth, and seventh years prior to the current date) would need to be preserved under the new standard. While the four-year policy has meant that the Company currently possesses records extending back to approximately September 2021, the Company would need to retain records through at least April 2019 (seven years prior to the Phase 2 effective date) in order to be fully compliant upon the effective date --- and many of those older records may still exist on archived media.

310	
311	The Cascade HCM Platform v4.2 has a configurable retention period for active, online records. This parameter is currently set to four (4) years, consistent with the Company\'s existing retention policy. Records that exceed the four-year retention window are automatically archived to offline tape storage maintained by Oakvale Point Software, Inc. at its data center facility in Round Rock, Texas.

313	Records residing on offline tape storage present two critical deficiencies under the new statute:

This process typically takes five to ten business days, depending on the volume of records requested, the availability of the data services team, and the physical location of the tape within the archive.**

329	**[VIII. Employee Handbook --- Anti-Retaliation Policy Status]{.underline}**
330	
331	This section assesses the adequacy of the Company\'s current anti-retaliation policy as set forth in the Employee Handbook, measured against the specific requirements of SB 2847 Phase 1 (effective January 1, 2026).
332	
333	**VIII.A. Current Policy (Handbook Section 9.4)**
334	
335	The Omnicron Employee Handbook was last comprehensively updated in **March 2023**. No interim supplements, amendments, or addenda have been issued since that date. The handbook is distributed to all new hires during onboarding and is available electronically through the Company\'s internal SharePoint portal.
336	
337	Section 9.4 of the handbook, titled \"Anti-Retaliation Policy,\" is a general, broadly worded provision that reads, in relevant part, as follows:
338	
339	> *\"Omnicron Logistics is committed to maintaining a workplace free from retaliation. No employee will be subjected to adverse employment action for reporting, in good faith, any violation of law or company policy, or for participating in any investigation of such violations. Employees who believe they have experienced retaliation should report the matter to their supervisor or to the Human Resources Department.\"*
340	
341	While this language communicates the Company\'s general anti-retaliation commitment, it does **not** satisfy the specificity requirements of SB 2847 Phase 1. Specifically, the current policy fails to include the following elements:
342	
343	1\. **No specific reference to wage and hour complaints or inquiries about wages.** The current policy addresses \"violations of law or company policy\" in general terms but does not specifically identify wage and hour complaints, wage inquiries, or any conduct protected under the Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act or SB 2847 as protected activities. The new statute requires that the anti-retaliation policy specifically address wage-related protected activities.
344	
345	2\. **No reference to the Illinois Wage Payment and Collection Act or SB 2847.** The current policy does not cite any specific statute. SB 2847 requires that the employer\'s anti-retaliation notice reference the Act by name and inform employees of their rights under the new statute.
346	
347	3\. **No enumeration of specific protected activities.** Phase 1 requires that the anti-retaliation policy enumerate the following specific protected activities: (a) inquiring about one\'s own wages or the wages of other employees; (b) disclosing one\'s own wages; (c) filing a complaint with the Illinois Department of Labor; (d) participating in or cooperating with an IDOL investigation or proceeding; and (e) testifying in any proceeding related to the Act. The current policy\'s reference to \"reporting violations\" and \"participating in investigations\" is insufficiently specific to satisfy this requirement.
348	
349	4\. **No statement of available remedies.** The current policy does not inform employees of the specific remedies available to them if they experience retaliation. SB 2847 provides that employees who are subjected to retaliation may be entitled to reinstatement, back pay, compensatory damages, and attorneys\' fees. The policy must communicate these potential remedies to employees.
350	
351	5\. **No acknowledgment mechanism.** The current policy does not include a signature line or other mechanism for confirming that the employee has received and reviewed the anti-retaliation notice. While the handbook generally includes an acknowledgment of receipt form signed during onboarding, that form is a general acknowledgment of the entire handbook and does not constitute specific acknowledgment of the anti-retaliation provisions as required by the Act.

355	Phase 1 of SB 2847, effective January 1, 2026, requires that the Act\'s anti-retaliation protections be \"specifically communicated to all employees in writing\" and that the employer maintain records demonstrating that each employee has received the required notice. If IDOL does not publish templates in Polish and Tagalog before the January 1, 2026 effective date, determine whether the Company must commission its own certified translations of the English-language notice. As discussed in Section III.B, this interpretive question should be referred to outside counsel.

This estimate includes professional translation costs for any languages not covered by IDOL-published templates, printing in poster format, and installation at each facility.

393	**[X. Temporary Staffing Agency Arrangements --- FlexForce Overview]{.underline}**
394	
395	This section provides a factual overview of the Company\'s relationship with FlexForce Staffing Solutions, LLC, the Company\'s primary temporary staffing agency provider for Illinois operations. The legal implications of this relationship under SB 2847\'s Phase 3 joint employer liability provisions are addressed in summary fashion only; a detailed analysis of the FlexForce arrangement and the required amendments to the Master Services Agreement are the subject of a separate workstream overseen by Priya Chakravarti\'s office.
396	
397	**Overview of the Relationship.** FlexForce Staffing Solutions, LLC is an Illinois limited liability company with its registered agent located at 220 North Wacker Drive, Suite 1100, Chicago, Illinois 60606. FlexForce provides temporary warehouse workers to Omnicron\'s Illinois facilities during peak demand periods --- typically the fourth-quarter holiday fulfillment season (October through January) and periodic promotional event surges throughout the year. At peak utilization, approximately **380 temporary workers** are assigned to Omnicron facilities across the eleven Illinois locations.
398	
399	The relationship is governed by a Master Services Agreement originally dated March 15, 2022, which was most recently amended by Amendment No. 1, dated January 8, 2024. FlexForce bills Omnicron at a rate of **\$22.50 per hour** per temporary worker. FlexForce pays the temporary workers a wage of **\$16.25 per hour**, resulting in a markup of \$6.25 per hour (approximately 38.5%). FlexForce is responsible for all payroll functions for the temporary workers, including wage payments, federal and state tax withholding, FICA contributions, and workers\' compensation insurance coverage.
400	
401	**Omnicron\'s Operational Involvement.** While FlexForce is the employer of record for the temporary workers, Omnicron exercises significant day-to-day operational control over these individuals during their assignments at Omnicron facilities. Specifically:
402	
403	> • Omnicron sets the shift schedules for temporary workers, including start times, end times, break periods, and overtime assignments.
404	>
405	> • Omnicron supervisors direct the temporary workers\' daily tasks, assigning them to specific workstations, picking zones, packing lines, and loading areas.
406	>
407	> • Omnicron facility managers have the authority to reject or remove individual temporary workers from the facility for performance, safety, or conduct reasons, without requiring FlexForce\'s prior approval.
408	
409	This level of operational control is relevant to the joint employer analysis under SB 2847 Phase 3, which imposes joint and several liability on client companies that exercise sufficient control over the terms and conditions of work performed by temporary staffing agency employees.
410	
411	**Compliance Verification Gap.** I note that the Company currently has **no mechanism** to verify that FlexForce is properly paying wages, maintaining the payroll records required under the Act, providing compliant pay stubs, or furnishing the required wage notices to the temporary workers who are assigned to Omnicron\'s facilities. The Master Services Agreement contains a general representation by FlexForce that it will comply with all applicable laws (Section 5.1), and an indemnification clause under which FlexForce agrees to indemnify Omnicron for losses arising from FlexForce\'s failure to comply with employment laws (Section 8.3, as revised by Amendment No. 1). However, there is no audit right, compliance reporting obligation, or verification mechanism that would allow Omnicron to confirm FlexForce\'s compliance on an ongoing basis.
412	
413	Under SB 2847\'s Phase 3 joint employer provisions, Omnicron may be held jointly and severally liable for FlexForce\'s wage and hour violations affecting the temporary workers assigned to Omnicron\'s facilities, regardless of the indemnification provision. I further note that Phase 3 includes a provision prohibiting contractual waiver or limitation of joint employer liability, which may render the existing indemnification clause in Section 8.3 unenforceable to the extent it purports to shift liability for statutory violations.
414	
415	I recommend that Priya Chakravarti review the FlexForce MSA indemnification clause in light of these provisions and that the Company implement compliance verification mechanisms --- such as periodic audit rights, monthly compliance certifications, or access to FlexForce\'s payroll records for Omnicron-assigned workers --- as part of a forthcoming amendment to the MSA. The primary contact at FlexForce for this discussion is Tamara Osgood, Vice President of Client Services.
416

For each gap, I have indicated the recommended priority level, the estimated cost (where quantifiable), and the responsible parties for remediation.

422	
423	**1. Pay Stub Deficiencies (Section IV)**

425	The Company\'s current pay stubs are missing five (5) data fields for hourly and non-exempt employees and two (2) data fields for salaried exempt employees. The critical-path constraint is Verdant\'s 10-to-12 week implementation timeline, which establishes **October 9, 2025** as the latest possible date for contract amendment execution. This is the single most time-sensitive item in this memorandum. Maximum annual penalty exposure for non-compliance: \$41,834,000.

427	**2. Anti-Retaliation Policy (Section VIII)**
428	
429	Handbook Section 9.4 must be revised to include specific references to wage and hour protections, the new statute, all enumerated protected activities, and available remedies. The revised policy must be distributed to all 3,218 Illinois employees with individual acknowledgments of receipt, translated into Spanish, Polish, and Tagalog (at the Waukegan facility), and incorporated into the onboarding process. Estimated training cost for HR staff and supervisors: \$42,000.

431	**3. Workplace Postings (Section IX)**
432	
433	Multilingual workplace postings must be displayed at all eleven Illinois facilities in English and Spanish, and in Polish and Tagalog at specific facilities where those language groups exceed 5% of the workforce. A per-facility language audit must be completed to confirm obligations at borderline facilities. The IDOL has not yet published the required notice template. Estimated cost: \$8,500.

435	**Recommended Responsible Parties for Phase 1:** Angela Fontaine and Jason Reeves at Verdant (payroll system upgrade); Derek Winstead (handbook revision, workplace posting, language audit); Priya Chakravarti (Verdant contract approval, legal review of handbook revisions); Nora Ellsworth at Hargrove, Tillman & Bates LLP (legal review and statutory guidance).

437	**XI.B. Phase 2 --- April 1, 2026**

439	**4. Wage Notice Forms (Section V)**

The open question of whether distribution to all 3,218 current employees is required (or only to new hires and employees with compensation changes) must be resolved by counsel. Estimated development and distribution cost: \$34,000.

443	**5. Recordkeeping Retention and Accessibility (Section VII)**
444	
445	The Cascade HCM Platform retention period must be extended from four (4) years to seven (7) years, and existing records currently archived to offline tape storage must be migrated to a searchable online format capable of production within 72 hours of an IDOL request. Estimated cost for the Oakvale Point Software reconfiguration and data migration project: \$67,000.

447	**Recommended Responsible Parties for Phase 2: Angela Fontaine (Oakvale Point Software work order, wage notice cost management); Derek Winstead (retention policy update, wage notice form development and distribution); Priya Chakravarti (resolution of retroactivity question via outside counsel).**

449	**XI.C. Phase 3 --- July 1, 2026**

451	**6. Independent Contractor Driver Classification (Section VI)**

462	
463	Phase 4 of SB 2847 activates the Act\'s private right of action provisions, including **treble damages** for willful violations, **class and collective action** mechanisms, and **mandatory attorneys\' fee shifting** in favor of prevailing employees. 465	I note that the Act includes a **60-day safe harbor cure period** for pay stub and wage notice violations. Under this provision, an employer that discovers a deficiency in its pay stubs or wage notices may self-report the deficiency to the Illinois Department of Labor and cure the violation within 60 days without incurring penalties, provided that (a) the employer self-reports before any employee complaint has been filed with IDOL or any court, and (b) the employer makes affected employees whole by providing corrected pay stubs or wage notices and paying any underpayment of wages. This safe harbor may serve as a strategic backstop for any Phase 1 or Phase 2 deficiencies that cannot be fully remediated before their respective effective dates, but it is available only if the Company acts proactively before a complaint triggers enforcement. I recommend that Priya Chakravarti discuss the potential use of this safe harbor mechanism with Nora Ellsworth as part of the overall compliance strategy.
466	
467	**[XII. Conclusion and Next Steps]{.underline}**
468	
469	The compliance challenges presented by SB 2847 are substantial, spanning virtually every aspect of the Company\'s HR, payroll, and employment practices in Illinois. However, these challenges are manageable if addressed with appropriate urgency, adequate resources, and coordinated effort across the HR, legal, and finance functions.

Failure to meet this deadline will almost certainly result in non-compliance with Phase 1 pay stub requirements on January 1, 2026, with potential penalty exposure exceeding \$41 million annually. I urge that this item receive the General Counsel\'s immediate attention.

473	I respectfully request that a meeting be convened with Priya Chakravarti, Angela Fontaine, Marcus Delaney, and me by no later than **October 1, 2025** to align on compliance priorities, authorize the necessary expenditures, and establish a project timeline with clear milestones and accountability for each Phase.

475	I further recommend that Nora Ellsworth at Hargrove, Tillman & Bates LLP be formally engaged immediately to provide the statutory analysis, the independent contractor classification legal opinion, the FlexForce MSA review, and guidance on the handbook revision. Several of the interpretive questions flagged in this memorandum --- including the retroactivity of wage notices, the multilingual obligation in the absence of IDOL-published templates, and the scope of the ABC test prongs as applied to the Company\'s driver model --- require authoritative legal analysis that is beyond the scope of this internal HR audit.

17	Mr. Speaker, this legislation represents a comprehensive overhaul of how Illinois protects working people from wage theft, misclassification, and exploitation. I want to briefly walk my colleagues through the structure of the bill before we proceed to questions.
18	
19	SB 2847 employs a four-phase effective date structure designed to give employers adequate time to come into compliance. Phase 1, effective January 1, 2026, activates the pay stub disclosure requirements, the anti-retaliation protections, and the workplace posting obligations. Phase 2, effective April 1, 2026, activates the wage notice requirements at the time of hire, the direct deposit option for employees, and the new recordkeeping requirements, including a seven-year retention period for all payroll records. Phase 3, effective July 1, 2026, activates joint employer liability provisions, the ABC test for independent contractor classification, and the new penalty framework. Phase 4, effective October 1, 2026, activates the private right of action with treble damages, attorney fee shifting, class action provisions, and the rulemaking authority for the Illinois Department of Labor.
20	
21	I want to focus the body\'s attention on the wage notice requirement under Phase 2. This provision is among the most critical worker protection provisions in this legislation. It is the intent of this body that the wage notice requirement apply not only to new hires on and after the effective date, but to all existing employees. Employers should provide the required wage notice to every current employee within 90 days of the April 1, 2026 effective date --- that is, no later than June 30, 2026.
22	
23	Let me describe what the wage notice must contain. Under Section 15(a), the employer must provide a written notice stating the employee\'s rate or rates of pay and the basis thereof --- whether hourly, salary, piece rate, or commission --- along with the employer\'s legal name and any \"doing business as\" name, the employer\'s Federal Employer Identification Number, the employer\'s physical address, the employer\'s telephone number, the employee\'s regular pay schedule, any allowances claimed as part of the minimum wage, the employee\'s paid leave accrual rate, and an acknowledgment signature from the employee confirming receipt.

If the Illinois Department of Labor has published a wage notice template in the employee\'s primary language, the employer must provide the notice in that language. Section 15(c) directs IDOL to publish templates in at least English, Spanish, Polish, Mandarin, Tagalog, and Arabic within 60 days of the Phase 2 effective date.

57	**REPRESENTATIVE SANDOVAL:** Mr. Speaker, I also want to address the safe harbor provision in Section 25 of SB 2847. We have included a 60-day safe harbor cure period for employers who discover they have pay stub deficiencies or wage notice violations. It does NOT apply to independent contractor misclassification under Section 20, joint employer violations under Section 22, or anti-retaliation violations under Section 12. Those are too serious to allow a simple cure. The safe harbor is designed for good-faith employers who are working to come into compliance with the new disclosure requirements.
62	
63	**REPRESENTATIVE MURCHISON:** And what happens if an employer self-reports and then fails to cure within 60 days?
64	
65	**REPRESENTATIVE SANDOVAL:** If the employer does not cure within the 60-day window, the standard penalties apply retroactively to the original violation date. The safe harbor is not an extension --- it is an opportunity. Employers must take it seriously. We set the penalty for pay stub violations at \$500 per employee per pay period, and for wage notice failures at \$1,000 per employee. These are intentionally significant. For a large employer with thousands of workers, non-compliance could result in penalties in the tens of millions of dollars. The safe harbor is the off-ramp we are providing. Employers who act in good faith should use it.

68

71	**REPRESENTATIVE SANDOVAL:** I now want to address the Phase 4 provisions taking effect October 1, 2026. For too long, wage theft has been treated as a cost of doing business. When an employer steals wages from a worker, the worst that happens is they pay back what they owed. That is not a deterrent --- that is a loan. Under this Act, beginning October 1, 2026, any worker whose wages have been unlawfully withheld may bring a private action and recover three times the amount of unpaid wages, plus reasonable attorney\'s fees and costs. We are also enabling class and collective actions so that workers are not forced to fight alone. A single warehouse worker making sixteen dollars an hour should not have to hire a lawyer to recover two hundred dollars in unpaid overtime. Class actions level the playing field.

73	**REPRESENTATIVE MURCHISON:** Isn\'t treble damages excessive? Won\'t this invite frivolous litigation against employers who make honest payroll mistakes?
74	
75	**REPRESENTATIVE SANDOVAL:** That is precisely why we have the staggered effective dates and the safe harbor. Employers have from the date of signing --- September 12 of this year --- until October 1, 2026, more than a full year, to get their houses in order. Phase 1 starts January 1. Phase 2, April 1. Phase 3, July 1. The private right of action does not activate until Phase 4 on October 1, 2026. Any employer that has not achieved compliance in over twelve months is not making an honest mistake --- they are making a choice. I also want to note that the attorney fee-shifting provision is mandatory for prevailing employees but discretionary for prevailing employers, consistent with federal civil rights fee-shifting standards. This ensures that workers are not deterred from asserting their rights by the fear of paying the employer\'s legal fees if they lose.

Employees may bring private actions for unpaid wages with treble damages. The two tracks are complementary, not mutually exclusive. However, an employee may not recover both IDOL-assessed penalties and treble damages for the same violation --- that would constitute an impermissible double recovery.

Under the ABC test, a worker is presumed to be an employee unless the hiring entity demonstrates all three prongs: A --- the worker is free from control and direction in the performance of the work, both under the contract and in fact; B --- the work is performed outside the usual course of the hiring entity\'s business; and C --- the worker is customarily engaged in an independently established trade, occupation, or business of the same nature as the work performed.

This Act expands the ABC test to cover all wage and hour provisions, including minimum wage, overtime, pay stub requirements, wage notices, and recordkeeping. It closes a significant gap. The penalty for misclassification under Section 20 is \$2,500 per misclassified worker per quarter.

209	**11.1 Governing Law.** This Amendment and the Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Illinois, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. The Parties agree that the Uniform Commercial Code shall not apply to this Agreement.

215	**11.4 Waiver.** No waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument signed by the waiving Party. 216

13	**RECITALS**
14	
15	**WHEREAS**, Company is a third-party logistics and warehousing company that provides delivery and distribution services to its clients throughout the State of Illinois;
16	
17	**WHEREAS**, Company desires to engage Contractor to perform delivery services on behalf of Company and its clients in connection with Company\'s logistics and distribution operations; and

21	**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
22	
23	**[Section 1: Engagement and Services]{.underline}**
24	
25	**1.1 Engagement.** Company hereby engages Contractor, and Contractor hereby accepts such engagement, as an independent contractor to perform last-mile delivery services within Company\'s Illinois service territory, as more particularly described in this Section 1 (the \"Services\"). Contractor\'s engagement shall be subject to all terms and conditions of this Agreement.
26	
27	**1.2 Scope of Services.** Contractor shall perform pickup and delivery of packages, parcels, and freight from Company\'s warehouse and distribution facilities to designated delivery locations as assigned by Company. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Contractor shall complete delivery routes generated and assigned by Company\'s proprietary routing software system (\"RouteLogix\") each service day. Contractor shall be responsible for the safe handling, transport, and timely delivery of all packages, parcels, and freight assigned to Contractor\'s route. Contractor shall scan all packages upon pickup from the warehouse facility and upon delivery at each designated stop using the RouteLogix mobile application.
28	
29	**1.3 Service Territory.** Contractor shall perform Services within the geographic areas designated by Company from time to time, which may include deliveries originating from any of Company\'s eleven (11) Illinois warehouse and distribution facilities located in DuPage, Will, Cook, Kane, Lake, and Winnebago counties. Company reserves the right to modify the designated service territory upon reasonable notice to Contractor as operational needs require.
30	
31	**1.4 Route Assignments.** Company shall generate and provide Contractor with daily delivery route assignments via the RouteLogix platform no later than 5:00 AM on each scheduled service day. Each route assignment shall specify the pickup facility, the sequence of delivery stops, the estimated mileage, and the anticipated delivery time windows for each stop. Contractor shall follow the route sequence and delivery order as generated by RouteLogix unless deviation is required by road conditions, emergency, or customer unavailability. Any deviation from the assigned route must be reported to Company\'s dispatch center within thirty (30) minutes of the deviation, together with the reason therefor. Company\'s dispatch center shall be available during all Service Windows to provide guidance and updated routing instructions as needed.
32	
33	**[Section 2: Schedule and Availability]{.underline}**
34	
35	**2.1 Scheduled Service Windows.** Contractor shall be available to perform Services during the following scheduled shift windows as designated by Company: 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Saturday (each, a \"Service Window\"). Company shall assign Contractor to specific Service Windows on a weekly basis, provided that Company shall give Contractor no less than forty-eight (48) hours\' advance notice of each weekly schedule assignment. Weekly schedule assignments shall be communicated through the RouteLogix platform or by such other means as Company may designate.
36	
37	**2.2 Minimum Availability.** Contractor agrees to make himself or herself available for a minimum of five (5) Service Windows per week during each week of the term of this Agreement. Failure to meet the minimum availability requirement for three (3) or more consecutive weeks shall constitute grounds for termination of this Agreement under Section 9.4.
38	
39	**2.3 Scheduling.** While Company and Contractor shall endeavor to accommodate Contractor\'s scheduling preferences to the extent reasonably practicable, Company retains the right to assign Service Windows based on operational needs, delivery volume, and client requirements. Contractor may decline a specific assigned Service Window no more than twice per calendar month without penalty. Declinations in excess of two (2) per calendar month shall be documented and may be considered in evaluating Contractor\'s continued engagement.
40	
41	**2.4 Attendance and Punctuality.** Contractor shall report to the designated Company facility at the start of each assigned Service Window to receive route assignments, load delivery vehicles, and commence deliveries. Late arrival exceeding fifteen (15) minutes past the start of the assigned Service Window shall be documented by Company\'s facility supervisor and may result in route reassignment, reduction in delivery stops for the service day, or termination under Section 9.4. Contractor shall notify Company\'s dispatch center as soon as reasonably practicable if Contractor anticipates being unable to report for an assigned Service Window.
42	
43	**[Section 3: Compensation]{.underline}**
44	
45	**3.1 Per-Stop Compensation.** Company shall pay Contractor Four Dollars and Seventy-Five Cents (\$4.75) for each completed delivery stop (the \"Per-Stop Rate\"). For purposes of this Agreement, a \"completed delivery stop\" means a delivery attempted at a designated address, whether or not the recipient accepts delivery, provided Contractor follows Company\'s delivery attempt protocols as set forth in the Operations Manual, including obtaining proof of attempt through the RouteLogix mobile application.
46	
47	**3.2 Mileage Supplement.** In addition to the Per-Stop Rate, Company shall pay Contractor Thirty-Eight Cents (\$0.38) per mile driven while performing Services, as calculated by Company\'s RouteLogix system based on the assigned route mileage (the \"Mileage Supplement\"). The Mileage Supplement shall be computed using the RouteLogix-generated route distance for each assigned delivery route. Actual mileage deviations from the RouteLogix-calculated mileage shall not be compensated unless such deviations are pre-approved by Company\'s dispatch center and documented in the RouteLogix system.
48	
49	**3.3 Payment Terms.** Compensation shall be calculated on a bi-weekly basis and paid within ten (10) business days following the end of each two-week service period. Payment shall be made by check or electronic funds transfer to the account designated by Contractor on the attached Payment Information Form (Exhibit B). Company shall provide Contractor with a written or electronic statement of compensation earned for each pay period, itemizing the number of completed stops, route miles, and total compensation.
50	
51	**3.4 No Minimum Guarantee.** Contractor acknowledges and agrees that compensation under this Agreement is based solely on completed delivery stops and miles driven as calculated by the RouteLogix system. Company does not guarantee any minimum number of stops, miles, or earnings per Service Window, per week, or per pay period. The number of stops and miles available to Contractor will depend on delivery volume, client requirements, seasonal demand, and other operational factors as determined by Company.
52	
53	**3.5 No Withholding.** Company shall not withhold any federal, state, or local income taxes, Social Security taxes, Medicare taxes, unemployment insurance contributions, or any other payroll taxes from amounts paid to Contractor under this Agreement. Contractor is solely responsible for all tax obligations arising from compensation received under this Agreement, including but not limited to the timely payment of all federal and state income taxes and self-employment taxes. Company shall issue an IRS Form 1099-NEC to Contractor for each calendar year in which total payments to Contractor exceed Six Hundred Dollars (\$600).
54	
55	**3.6 No Benefits.** Contractor shall not be eligible for, and shall not participate in, any Company employee benefit plans, programs, or arrangements, including but not limited to health insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, retirement plans (401(k) or otherwise), paid time off, sick leave, disability insurance, workers\' compensation insurance, life insurance, or any other employee benefits provided by Company to its employees. Contractor acknowledges that Contractor\'s engagement as an independent contractor does not entitle Contractor to any such benefits.
56	
57	**[Section 4: Vehicle and Equipment]{.underline}**
58	
59	**4.1 Company Vehicle.** Contractor shall perform Services using a delivery vehicle provided by Company under a separate Vehicle Lease Agreement between Contractor and Company (the \"Vehicle Lease\"), a copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference. The leased vehicle shall bear Company branding, logos, and livery as specified by Company, and Contractor shall not alter, remove, obscure, or cover such branding at any time during the term of this Agreement. Contractor shall use the leased vehicle exclusively for the performance of Services under this Agreement and shall not use the vehicle for personal purposes or for the provision of services to any other party.
60	
61	**4.2 Vehicle Maintenance.** Contractor shall maintain the leased vehicle in good working condition and in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local motor vehicle laws and regulations. Company shall be responsible for major mechanical repairs and scheduled preventive maintenance, which shall be performed at Company-designated service facilities. Contractor shall be responsible for fueling the vehicle, keeping the vehicle clean and presentable, and performing daily pre-trip vehicle inspections using Company\'s Vehicle Inspection Checklist (Form OL-VI-03). Contractor shall promptly report any mechanical issues, damage, or safety concerns to Company\'s fleet management department.
62	
63	**4.3 Uniforms and Appearance.** Contractor shall, while performing Services, wear the Company-issued uniform consisting of: (a) an Omnicron Logistics-branded polo shirt or jacket, (b) an Omnicron Logistics-branded cap, and (c) khaki or black pants (Contractor-provided). Company shall provide the branded apparel at no charge to Contractor. Contractor shall maintain a neat and professional appearance at all times while performing Services, consistent with Company\'s Delivery Professional Appearance Standards as set forth in Appendix C to the Operations Manual.
64	
65	**4.4 Contractor-Supplied Equipment.** Contractor shall supply, at Contractor\'s own expense, the following equipment necessary for the performance of Services: (a) a mobile phone capable of running the RouteLogix mobile application and maintaining a cellular data connection throughout each Service Window, and (b) a hand truck or delivery dolly suitable for package handling and transport.
66	
67	**4.5 GPS Tracking.** The Company vehicle provided under the Vehicle Lease is equipped with GPS tracking and telematics systems that record vehicle location, speed, idle time, and driving behavior. Contractor acknowledges and consents to continuous GPS monitoring of the vehicle during Service Windows for purposes of route optimization, delivery verification, safety compliance, and performance evaluation. Data collected through the GPS and telematics systems shall be the property of Company.

70	
71	**5.1 Delivery Protocols.** Contractor shall perform all deliveries in strict accordance with Company\'s Standard Delivery Protocols as set forth in the Company Operations Manual, as such manual may be amended, supplemented, or updated by Company from time to time. Contractor shall obtain proof of delivery---either an electronic signature from the recipient or photographic confirmation of package placement---for each delivery stop using the RouteLogix mobile application. Contractor shall follow all package handling procedures specified in the Operations Manual, including proper scanning, sorting, and securing of packages in the delivery vehicle.
72	
73	**5.2 Customer Service Standards.** Contractor shall adhere to Company\'s Customer Service Standards as set forth in the Operations Manual, including but not limited to: maintaining professional and courteous communication with all delivery recipients, handling of damaged or refused packages per Company protocol, timely reporting of delivery exceptions through the RouteLogix platform on the same day they occur, and following Company-specified procedures for delivery reattempts and package returns.
74	
75	**5.3 Training.** Prior to commencing Services under this Agreement, Contractor shall complete Company\'s Delivery Driver Orientation Program, which consists of approximately sixteen (16) hours of instruction covering delivery protocols, RouteLogix system operation, vehicle safety, package handling, and customer service standards. Contractor shall also complete annual refresher training as required and scheduled by Company. Training shall be provided at no cost to Contractor; however, Contractor shall not be compensated for time spent attending or completing any training sessions.
76	
77	**5.4 Performance Standards.** Contractor shall maintain a minimum delivery completion rate of ninety-seven percent (97%) and a minimum customer satisfaction rating of 4.2 out of 5.0 as measured by Company\'s post-delivery customer survey system. Performance metrics shall be reviewed by Company on a monthly basis. Failure to maintain these minimum performance standards for two (2) consecutive calendar months shall constitute grounds for immediate termination of this Agreement under Section 9.4.
78	
79	**5.5 Exclusivity.** During the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall not provide delivery, courier, or last-mile logistics services for any direct competitor of Company within Company\'s Illinois service territory without the prior written consent of Company. For purposes of this Section, a \"direct competitor\" means any person or entity engaged in third-party logistics, parcel delivery, or last-mile distribution services operating within DuPage, Will, Cook, Kane, Lake, or Winnebago counties, Illinois.

83	**6.1 Independent Contractor Relationship.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that Contractor is an independent contractor and is not an employee, agent, partner, or joint venturer of Company. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to create an employer-employee relationship between Company and Contractor. 84	
85	**6.2 No Authority to Bind.** Contractor shall have no authority to bind Company to any contract, agreement, obligation, or commitment, or to make any representation or warranty on behalf of Company, except as expressly authorized in writing by an authorized officer of Company.

87	**6.3 Method and Manner.** Contractor retains the right to determine the method, manner, and means by which Services are performed, subject to the delivery of results meeting Company\'s quality, safety, and operational standards as set forth in this Agreement and the Operations Manual. Company\'s interest is in the results to be achieved, and Contractor shall have discretion in determining the details of performance consistent with such standards.
88	
89	**6.4 Right to Hire Assistants.** Contractor may, at Contractor\'s own expense, hire helpers, assistants, or subcontractors to assist in performing Services under this Agreement, provided that any such helper, assistant, or subcontractor: (a) is approved in advance and in writing by Company; (b) satisfies Company\'s background check and drug screening requirements at Contractor\'s expense; (c) completes Company\'s Delivery Driver Orientation Program prior to performing any Services; and (d) agrees in writing to be bound by all applicable terms of this Agreement and Company\'s Operations Manual. Contractor shall remain fully responsible for the performance and conduct of any such helper, assistant, or subcontractor.
90	
91	**6.5 Tax Obligations.** Contractor acknowledges and accepts sole responsibility for the payment of all federal, state, and local taxes arising from compensation received under this Agreement, including without limitation all self-employment taxes, estimated tax payments, and any other tax liabilities. Contractor shall provide Company with a completed IRS Form W-9 (Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification) upon execution of this Agreement, and shall promptly notify Company of any changes to the information provided therein.
92	
93	**6.6 Insurance.** Contractor shall obtain and maintain, at Contractor\'s own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement: (a) commercial general liability insurance with minimum coverage limits of One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) in the aggregate; and (b) commercial automobile insurance with minimum coverage of One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) combined single limit per occurrence. 95	**[Section 7: Confidentiality]{.underline}**
96	
97	**7.1 Confidential Information.** Contractor acknowledges that, in the course of performing Services, Contractor may have access to and become acquainted with confidential and proprietary information belonging to Company (\"Confidential Information\"). Confidential Information includes, without limitation, customer lists, delivery volumes, pricing and rate structures, routing algorithms, the RouteLogix software and system architecture, operational data, business plans, marketing strategies, financial information, and any other information that is not generally known to the public and that derives economic value from its confidential nature. 99	**7.2 Survival.** The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section 7 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of two (2) years from the date of such expiration or termination.

101	**7.3 Return of Materials.** Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Contractor shall promptly return to Company all documents, materials, electronic files, and other property containing or relating to Confidential Information, including without limitation the Operations Manual and any copies thereof.

105	**8.1 Indemnification by Contractor.** Contractor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Company and its officers, directors, employees, agents, and affiliates from and against any and all claims, demands, actions, suits, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or relating to: (a) Contractor\'s performance of Services under this Agreement; (b) any act or omission of Contractor, Contractor\'s employees, helpers, assistants, or subcontractors; (c) any personal injury or property damage occurring in connection with the performance of Services; (d) any traffic violation, accident, or motor vehicle incident involving Contractor or the leased vehicle; or (e) any breach by Contractor of this Agreement.

117	**9.3 Termination for Convenience.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement at any time, with or without cause, upon fourteen (14) days\' prior written notice to the other Party. No penalty or termination fee shall be assessed against either Party in connection with a termination for convenience under this Section 9.3.
118

27	**9.4.2 --- Scope and Applicability**
28	
29	This Anti-Retaliation Policy applies to all employees of Omnicron Logistics, Inc., including full-time, part-time, and temporary employees. The policy covers all Omnicron facilities, operations, warehouse locations, distribution centers, and administrative offices, wherever situated. All levels of management and staff are subject to the obligations and protections set forth in this Section.
30	
31	Every employee, from entry-level personnel to senior executives, bears a responsibility to refrain from retaliatory conduct and to report any suspected retaliation observed in the workplace. Managers and supervisors bear a heightened responsibility to foster a culture in which reporting is encouraged and protected.
32	
33	**9.4.3 --- Protected Activities**
34	
35	For purposes of this policy, \"Protected Activities\" include the following:
36	
37	> \(a\) Reporting a suspected violation of federal, state, or local law to a supervisor, manager, or the Human Resources Department;
38	>
39	> \(b\) Reporting a suspected violation of Company policy, including but not limited to the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics;
40	>
41	> \(c\) Cooperating with any internal investigation conducted by the Company, including investigations initiated by the Human Resources Department, the Legal Department, or the Internal Audit function;
42	>
43	> \(d\) Filing a complaint with any external governmental agency regarding workplace safety, including but not limited to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), or participating in any OSHA inspection or proceeding; and
44	>
45	> \(e\) Participating in any government-initiated audit, inspection, or inquiry directed at the Company\'s operations, including responding truthfully to questions posed by government auditors or investigators.
46	
47	An employee\'s activity is considered \"in good faith\" when the employee reasonably believes that a violation of law or Company policy has occurred or is occurring, even if the employee\'s belief is ultimately determined to be mistaken. Reports that are knowingly false or made with malicious intent are not protected under this policy and may themselves be grounds for disciplinary action.
48	
49	**9.4.4 --- Definition of Retaliation**
50	
51	\"Retaliation\" means any adverse employment action taken against an employee because of the employee\'s engagement in a Protected Activity as defined in Section 9.4.3 above. Examples of adverse employment actions constituting retaliation include, but are not limited to:
52	
53	> • Termination of employment;
54	>
55	> • Demotion or reduction in job title or responsibilities;
56	>
57	> • Suspension, whether paid or unpaid;
58	>
59	> • Reduction in scheduled hours or shift reassignment;
60	>
61	> • Reduction in pay or denial of a scheduled pay increase;
62	>
63	> • Involuntary reassignment to less desirable duties or work locations;
64	>
65	> • Issuance of a negative performance evaluation that is not based on legitimate, good-faith assessment of the employee\'s performance;
66	>
67	> • Threats, harassment, intimidation, or coercion directed at the reporting employee; and
68	>
69	> • Any other action that would dissuade a reasonable employee from engaging in a Protected Activity.
70	
71	Retaliation may be overt or subtle. The Company will evaluate claims of retaliation based on the totality of the circumstances, including the timing of the alleged adverse action relative to the Protected Activity.
72	
73	**9.4.5 --- Reporting Procedure**
74	
75	Any employee who believes that he or she has been subjected to retaliation in violation of this policy is encouraged to report the matter promptly through one or more of the following channels:
76	
77	> \(a\) **Direct Supervisor.** Employees may report suspected retaliation to their direct supervisor, unless the supervisor is the individual alleged to have engaged in the retaliatory conduct.
78	>
79	> \(b\) **Human Resources Department.** Employees may contact the Human Resources Department directly by reaching the Senior Director, Human Resources at the Company\'s headquarters. Reports may be made in person, by telephone, or in writing, and should be directed to:
80	>
81	> Omnicron Logistics, Inc. Human Resources Department 4500 West Industrial Parkway Romeoville, IL 60446
82	>
83	> \(c\) **Anonymous Ethics Hotline.** Employees may also report concerns anonymously through the Company\'s confidential ethics hotline at **1-888-555-0147**. The hotline is operated by an independent third-party service provider and is available twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week. Employees should be aware that anonymous reports, while accepted and taken seriously, may limit the Company\'s ability to conduct a thorough investigation.
84	
85	Reports may be made verbally or in writing. The Company encourages employees to provide as much detail as possible, including the identity of the individuals involved, the dates and nature of the alleged retaliatory conduct, and the Protected Activity believed to have prompted the retaliation.
86	
87	**9.4.6 --- Investigation and Resolution**
88	
89	The Company will promptly and thoroughly investigate all reports of retaliation made under this policy. Investigations will be conducted by the Human Resources Department or, at the discretion of the Vice President and General Counsel, by outside counsel retained for that purpose. The Company will endeavor to maintain the confidentiality of all parties involved to the extent practicable and consistent with a thorough investigation.
90	
91	Upon completion of the investigation, the Company will take appropriate corrective action against any individual found to have engaged in retaliation. Corrective action may include counseling, written warnings, suspension, demotion, or termination, depending on the severity and circumstances of the violation. The complaining employee will be notified that the investigation has been completed, although specific disciplinary outcomes applied to other employees may be kept confidential in accordance with Company policy. The Company will not tolerate retaliation against any individual who participates in or cooperates with a retaliation investigation.
92	
93	**9.4.7 --- Consequences for Violations**
94	
95	Any employee found to have engaged in retaliation in violation of this policy will be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including immediate termination of employment. The severity of the disciplinary response will be determined based on the nature of the retaliatory conduct, the impact on the affected employee, and any prior history of similar violations.
96	
97	Managers and supervisors who fail to report known or suspected retaliation occurring within their departments, or who permit retaliatory conduct to continue without taking reasonable steps to intervene, may themselves be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination. Nothing in this Section shall be construed to limit any legal remedies that may be available to employees under applicable law.

    # **bold** markup

    for i, s in enumerate(parts):
        if not s: continue
        r = p.add_run(s)
        if i % 2 == 1: r.bold = True
    return p

    p = d.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else d.add_paragraph()

    if align == 'center': p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    if align == 'justify': p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    if size or italic:
        for r in p.runs:

    for i, h in enumerate(header):

            if hl and hl(ri, row): shade(c, 'FCE4E4')
            elif ri % 2 == 1: shade(c, 'F2F4F8')
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    d.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

        ("**Phase 2 — Apr 1, 2026**", "Wage notice at hire and on any change in rate, schedule or classification, with signed acknowledgment (§15-5); direct-deposit option with no fees (§15-10); 7-year retention, producible within 72 hours (§15-15)", "No wage-notice form or change-notice process exists. **MEMORANDUM**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **TO:**                             Board of Directors, Omnicron Logistics, Inc.
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **CC:**                             Marcus Delaney, Chief Executive Officer; Priya Chakravarti, Vice President & General Counsel; Angela Fontaine, Controller; Derek Winstead, Senior Director, Human Resources; Nora Ellsworth, Hargrove, Tillman & Bates LLP

  **FROM:**                           Office of the General Counsel (draft for General Counsel review)

  **DATE:**                           September 29, 2025 (facts current through the latest document in the record, dated September 26, 2025)

  **RE:**                             Illinois Wage Theft Prevention and Worker Protection Act (SB 2847) --- Compliance Timeline, Critical Path, Exposure and Board Decisions Required
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# I. Bottom Line for the Board

SB 2847 was signed on September 12, 2025 and phases in over four effective dates: **January 1, April 1, July 1 and October 1, 2026**. The internal HR audit (September 25, 2025) shows that Omnicron has a compliance gap under every phase. The gaps can be closed on time, but only if three things happen in the next 120 days: a payroll-vendor contract is signed within days, the Board takes ownership of the delivery-driver decision well before the February 2026 meeting proposed by management, and the Company stops treating the statutory safe harbor as a fallback. The key conclusions are:

1.  **The payroll vendor contract is the first deadline, and the real deadline is earlier than the one in the record.** The Verdant Payroll Systems amendment must be signed by **Tuesday, October 7, 2025** (management's target). October 9 is the last possible date. Verdant's 12-week schedule puts the \*first live pay cycle\* in week 12. Counted from October 9, that lands on January 1, 2026. Omnicron's first 2026 payday is probably **Friday, January 2, 2026**, and that payroll is processed in the last days of December. So October 9 leaves no buffer at all. Verdant itself says January 1 works only on its 10-week best case. HR's proposed December 15 completion guarantee cannot be met from an October 9 signing either: a 12-week build would have needed signature by September 22. If signature slips past mid-October, Verdant's fallback is a mid-February 2026 go-live. Under that fallback, Omnicron issues roughly 3--4 non-compliant payrolls, at **\$1,609,000 per pay period** (3,218 employees × \$500).

2.  **The Verdant scope is incomplete. Fix it before signing, not by change order.** Counsel's statutory summary lists required pay-stub fields that appear in neither the audit nor Verdant's preliminary scope: the last four digits of the SSN or an employee ID, the employer's telephone number, the date of payment, deductions itemized by category, and (to be confirmed) total hours and overtime \*rates\*. The audit also understates the exempt-employee gap. Appendix B to the audit itself shows three missing fields for exempt employees, not two. See Appendix B to this memorandum.

3.  **The delivery-driver model is the largest financial and legal exposure. It needs a Board decision by January 31, 2026, not at the February 2026 meeting.** On the facts in the record, the roughly 740 independent-contractor drivers are very unlikely to satisfy any prong of the ABC test that takes effect on **July 1, 2026**. Prong B (the work is outside the usual course of the business) is close to unwinnable for a logistics company that earns about 31% of its revenue from delivery. The HR audit also misstates a key fact: the Independent Contractor Agreement \*does\* contain an exclusivity clause (§5.5), and the vehicle may be used only for Omnicron (§4.1). Penalties run **per calendar quarter**. A transition that slips even one day past July 1 therefore incurs a full quarter's penalty of **\$1,850,000**. Implementation needs about five months, which requires a decision by the end of January.

4.  **The safe harbor i

173:The obligation is triggered by a language spoken as a primary language by **more than 5%** of the workforce at a particular site. On the survey data (Appendix A), the results are: Spanish is required at all 11 sites. Polish is required at 6 sites (Naperville, Elk Grove Village, Schaumburg, Mundelein, Rockford and Loves Park). Tagalog is required at Waukegan (11.9%). Note that Counsel Summary refers to "the Lake County facility", but Omnicron has two Lake County sites, and Mundelein is at 2.1%. **Correction:** the HR Audit counts Romeoville HQ as over the Polish threshold, but 26 of 520 is exactly 5.0%, which is not "more than 5%." Because the survey reached only 89.3% of employees, was offered only in English and Spanish, and appears to have counted non-respondents as English speakers, **we recommend posting in Polish at all 11 sites** (incremental cost is minimal) and completing the multilingual audit by mid-November. Tagalog is among the eight languages IDOL is directed to publish, so the HR Audit's concern about a missing Tagalog template should resolve once IDOL publishes. If IDOL misses its November 15 deadline, the Company should commission certified translations.

175-## B. Phase 2 (April 1, 2026)
176-
177-### 1. Wage notices: the retroactivity question
178-
179-The statutory text requires notices "at the time of hire and upon any change." The sponsor stated on the floor that existing employees should receive notices within 90 days of April 1 (that is, by June 30, 2026). Representatives Murchison and Kowalski objected on the record that the text does not say this, and no conforming amendment was adopted. IDOL cannot issue rules until Oct 1, 2026. **Working position: treat the notice as owed to all 3,218 existing employees, beginning distribution in March 2026 and finishing well before June 30, 2026.** The cost is modest (included in the \$34,000 line). The downside of the narrow reading is \$3.218M in penalties plus Phase 4 class exposure. The HR Audit's alternative target of "on or before April 1" is acceptable if it can be achieved, but nothing in the record requires it.
180-
181-**Language of notices.** The wage-notice language duty is tied to **each employee's primary language** where IDOL has published a template. It is not tied to the per-site 5% posting threshold. The HR Audit plans Tagalog notices only at Waukegan. Under the per-employee rule, all 42 Tagalog speakers, wherever they work, and any Mandarin or Arabic speakers would receive notices in their language once templates exist. The Floor Debate indicates that IDOL wage-notice templates are due within 60 days \*after\* April 1 (about May 31, 2026). Notices issued before then should be re-issued in the template language. **Change notices:** HR proposes giving notice \*before\* a change takes effect; the statute requires notice "upon" a change. HR's approach is the safer practice. Cascade should be configured so that every rate, shift-differential, schedule or classification change generates a notice. **Content:** the current offer letter lacks the FEIN, telephone number, specific payday, allowances statement ("none claimed"), leave-accrual rate and a separate acknowledgment.
182-
183-### 2. Recordkeeping and direct deposit
184-
185-Retention must move from 4 years (Policy HR-2021-004) to 7 years. Records on Oakvale tape take 5--10 business days to retrieve, which fails the 72-hour standard. Records requiring third-party vendor involvement are deemed non-compliant in any event. Actions: (i) change the Cascade retention parameter **now**, so that no further records age out to tape; (ii) migrate the existing tape records into searchable storage by March 1, 2026; (iii) suspend destruction immediately. To the extent records back to April 2019 have already been destroyed, document that fact. They cannot be recreated, and counsel should advise whether the 7-year rule reaches records created before April 1, 2026. Production rights must extend to FlexForce. MSA §5.1(c) currently allows Omnicron to inspect FlexForce records only on five business days' notice, which is inconsistent with a 72-hour production obligation once Omnicron is a joint employer. For direct deposit, confirm in writing that no facility requires direct deposit or charges check fees.

188-
189-### 1. Delivery drivers and the ABC test
190-
191-The record contains an unusually complete set of control facts. Several facts in the HR Audit are inconsistent with the governing Independent Contractor Agreement, and the Agreement is the more reliable source:

Omnicron-assigned 6 AM--6 PM windows, minimum 5 per week, no more than 2 declines per month (§§2.1--2.3). Lateness documented and can lead to termination (§2.4). Branded leased vehicle, uniforms, appearance standards, GPS monitoring (§§4.1, 4.3, 4.5). Operations Manual protocols; 97% completion and 4.2 rating metrics (§§5.1, 5.4). 16 hours of mandatory, unpaid training (§5.3). Very likely fails

203-**Options for the January Board decision.** (1) \*Reclassify as W-2 employees effective on or before July 1, 2026.\* Recomputed incremental cost is \$13.78M per year. That figure excludes overtime (illustratively \$5.1--\$8.4M per year, see Section VII), paid leave, 401(k), payroll administration and expense reimbursement (phones and hand trucks are now driver-supplied, and the mileage rate is \$0.38).    - The ~$38M driver overtime estimate likely uses the wrong method; a defensible range is about $5.1–$8.4M per year, pending the hours audit.
   - The $41.3M treble-damages figure trebles payroll taxes and premiums, which are not unpaid wages.
6. **The non-driver budget is about $614,350, not $485,500.** The HR memo and the Controller's spreadsheet reach the same total from different line items, and the "10%" contingency is actually 12%.
7. **Other errors in the documents:**
   - Romeoville HQ is exactly 5.0% Polish, so it does not cross the "more than 5%" threshold. The memo recommends posting in Polish at all sites anyway.
   - The language survey totals don't reconcile with the 344 non-respondents.
   - The FlexForce contract and the payroll-system vendor are identified inconsistently across the documents.
